titles: Put the creator first, then the bet or question in plain verbs, max 6 words. Never put the result in the title: 'Red Card', 'Copper' and 'Hang On' all gave away the payoff.
Phrase the stake as a question ('Can Kai Get Ray Through?'). Skip trivia ('Japan's Most Popular Dog') and vague teases ('Can't Believe What Happens').
Use one or two emoji at the end only. Drop stacks like 😭❤️‍🩹 and flags.
hooks: Max 6 words, and add the stake the narrator didn't. If the hook and narrator say the same thing, cut one.
Ask whether it happens; never announce the outcome ('ONE HIT AWAY', 'HIS NAME IS REALLY UP THERE'). State what's on the line ('LOSE AND THE STREAM ENDS').
Cut vague teases like 'WAIT FOR HIS LIFE ADVICE'. Every clip needs a hook and context line: OVl3TBtcYHo and JGopxMMkJo8 shipped with neither.
clip_picks: Only cut moments with a one-line spoken premise (bet, guess, countdown, question, argument). Speed or Kai with athletes and celebrities come first, then Kai with Ray.
Skip visual-only moments (crowds, dogs, clinches, boss-fight buildups, walk-ins). If it isn't funny read aloud, skip it.
One cut per moment. Three dubstep clips of the same scene is the clearest waste in this batch; pick the one with the named guest.
Mine Jynxzi rank guessing as a series, but state the premise in the first line.
length_and_pacing: Stop cutting every clip to 53s. Start ≤2s before the stake line, end ≤2s after the payoff, and aim for 15-30s. Most breakouts run 11-26s.
End on the payoff line and cut trailing banter so the clip loops.
posting: Post 1-2 clips a day within hours of the stream. Clips 5-7 days old compete with hundreds of other clippers and sit at 0 views.
Every clip sits at 0-18 views with n/a analytics, so check Studio for limits, duplicate-content flags and Shorts-feed serving. After 48h, judge on 3s retention and Shorts-feed share.
Confirm scheduled clips actually went public (bj9EzdPPHxI is still private).

money.idea: Paid clipping campaigns (N3on is the one known)
money.why: The channel already cuts Speed, Kai and Jynxzi clips. Campaign payouts depend on views, not subs or YPP, and with 0 subs and 42 views this is the only way to earn near-term.
money.first_step: Read the N3on campaign rules (allowed sources, length, required tags, payout basis) and cut one 15-30s clip that fits them. Submit it before scaling.

money.why: The format repeats, the premise fits in one line, and it can be a named series that builds subs.
money.first_step: Pick the next Jynxzi guessing-ranks stream, cut three premise-first clips under 30s with a series name in the hook, and post one a day.

money.idea: Fan-funding and ad revenue after the YPP thresholds
money.why: Fan funding needs 500 subs and Shorts views (42 of 3,000,000 now). Full YPP needs 1000 subs (0 now) and 10,000,000 Shorts views (42 now). Both are far off.
money.first_step: Track subs and 90-day Shorts views weekly in Studio, and check whether clips from creators' streams carry any reuse or monetization limits.

money.idea: Sponsor or affiliate links later, once the channel has an audience
money.why: With no audience there is nothing to sell yet. Once there is a consistent viewer base, a link in the description is cheap to add.
money.first_step: Don't pitch yet. Reach a baseline of a few thousand views per clip first, then pick one affiliate or sponsor fit.
